---
title: "D: on-policy distillation"
subtitle: "The student writes; the teacher grades every token"
---

{{< include /_setup.qmd >}}

**Question.** Does learning on its own answers, graded token by token by the teacher, beat copying
the teacher's text? ([Off-policy and on-policy](../concepts/on-policy.qmd).)

**Setup.** From the untrained 0.8B, every training query once: the student samples an answer at
temperature 1, the 2B scores every token of it, and the loss is the reverse KL over the whole
vocabulary. Gold is never read. TRL's `DistillationTrainer`, with the student sampling in vLLM next
to training and the teacher, on the 12 GB card.

::: {.facts}
```{python}
table(["D", "B"])
```
:::

```{ojs}
runs = ["D"]
```

{{< include /_run.qmd >}}

## What it shows

- **It ties B on xLAM, in a different way.** `{python} story.claim("D", "B", "test-clean")`. D is
  better at choosing functions and completing every call; B is better at xLAM's habit of writing
  defaults out (`{python} pct(M["defaults"]["B"]["default_made_explicit"], 0)` against
  `{python} pct(M["defaults"]["D"]["default_made_explicit"], 0)` on those rows).
- **On unseen tools it is above B's selected checkpoint**: `{python} story.score("D", "bfcl")` on
  BFCL (`{python} story.claim("D", "B", "bfcl")`), and not significantly different from the 2B. But
  its BFCL rises with training, and B's keeps rising past its own pick to a score D doesn't
  significantly beat, so with one seed the data can't tell on-policy learning from more training.
- **Per GPU-hour it shows no advantage.** At B's budget (step `{python} d_budget["step"]`,
  `{python} f"{d_budget['gpu_hours']:.1f}"` GPU-hours) it scores
  `{python} pct(d_budget["official"]["test-clean"]["exact"])` on test-clean
  (`{python} story.claim(f"D@{d_budget['step']}", "B", "test-clean")`). Its selected checkpoint cost
  `{python} story.gpu_hours("D")` GPU-hours.
